recordDecisions.title: On the local geometry of the tight 39-point code in 𝕆P²
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
Cohn, Kumar and Minton constructed a universally optimal code of thirty-nine points in the octonionic projective plane 𝕆P², whose existence was conjectured by Hoggar. Its points form thirteen mutually unbiased Jordan frames, and a four-parameter phase family deforms the code through such configurations. This Lean development describes their local geometry under the automorphism group F₄. At every nonresonant phase, every nearby real solution of the defining equations belongs to one of four smooth families of labelled configurations. In a local slice for F₄, their union has normal form R⁴ × ⋃ᵢ₌₁⁴ R⁶ᵢ, with the R⁶ᵢ in direct sum. The distance to the localized family union is bounded by a phase-dependent constant times the square root of the residual, and the exponent 1/2 is sharp in the ambient configuration space. On an explicit open dense subset of the nonresonant phases, the complexified families are exactly the top-dimensional components of the complex solution germ, each generically reduced. Every neighbourhood of the original code in the space of unlabelled tight 39-point codes modulo F₄ contains points of local dimension 10.

The results are local, the resonant germ at the original code is not classified, and lower-dimensional complex components are not excluded. For exact frames and strongly convex C² overlap potentials, we prove a two-sided comparison of the energy gap with squared overlap errors and, near each nonresonant orbit, a quartic lower bound in distance to the localized family union. Except for attributed third-party material, all text and code are AI-generated under Robert R. MacGregor’s direction. Robert is an amateur who welcomes collaboration (macgregor@gmail.com).

recordDecisions.title: QuadraticFloor: quadratic floor sums and the trace of a quartic Bernoulli number
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: For an odd prime p and integers A, B, C, the alternating floor sum S_{A,B,C}(p) is the sum over 0 <= n < p of (-1)^floor((A n^2 + B n + C)/p). The development proves the root-count reduction of S_{A,B,C}(p) to a sum of Legendre symbols over an arithmetic progression when A + B is even, and, for a positive odd A, an odd prime p not dividing A and an admissible pair (B odd, prime to A, 1 <= B^2 - 4AC < 4A), the square-class decomposition: S_{A,B,C}(p) equals (-1)^C minus the average over the Dirichlet characters psi modulo A of conj(psi(B))^2 times the first Bernoulli number, at modulus 8Ap, of the odd character eta_p chi_{-4}^{delta} psi, where eta_p is the Kronecker character of discriminant -8p. Consequently the sum depends only on the square class of B modulo A. At A = 1 and A = 3 this gives the floor sums in terms of Bernoulli numbers of quadratic characters (which are class numbers by Dirichlet's formula, not formalized). At A = 5 the difference S_{5,3,0}(p) - S_{5,1,0}(p) is the real part of the first Bernoulli number of the quartic character Theta_p = eta_p chi_{-4} xi of conductor 40p, with xi(2) = i; this real part is an even integer whose residue modulo 4 is given by an explicit indicator z_1 - z_3. Finally the sums with A = 1 and fixed shifts a, b are classified: for odd a in terms of S_{1,1,0}(p) and an oriented sum of Legendre symbols, for even a by an explicit finite formula that is bounded and eventually constant in p.

recordDecisions.title: Linked-site block laws of all lengths identify the collapsed mutation-scaled genealogy
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: This entry formalizes an identifiability theorem for three sampled sequences whose sites all share one random three-tip genealogy (complete linkage). A genealogy is a pair of branch lengths (u, v), where u is the height of the cherry and v is the length of the upper internal branch, together with a label in Fin 3 recording which pair of tips forms the cherry. Its law is an arbitrary finite measure that is almost everywhere supported on nonnegative branch lengths. Given the genealogy, sites evolve independently under the K-state equal-rates mutation model with a uniform root distribution and mutation scale k. For K ≥ 2 and k, l ≥ 0, two such measures, with scales k and l, produce the same law of block patterns for every number L of linked sites if and only if their collapsed objects agree. The collapsed object is the push-forward of the measure under (u, v, q) ↦ (k u, k v, q), with the cherry label replaced by a fixed value whenever k v = 0. A second statement shows that, for a genealogy with zero upper branch (a star tree), the block-pattern law does not depend on which cherry label is attached.

recordDecisions.title: Total variation bound between an unpruned ancestral recombination process and SMC' on pairwise coalescence times
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: This entry formalizes a total variation bound between the pairwise coalescence-time process of an unpruned ancestral recombination graph and the SMC' approximation, for N ≥ 1 samples, a unit-length genome, and scaled recombination rate R ≥ 0. The observed object is the collection of pairwise coalescence times of all sample pairs at every rational position in [0, 1). The total variation distance is at most an explicit double bound, which is at most min(1, R² times a quadratic coefficient in N − 1). The distance is 0 for one sample and for zero recombination. Supporting statements show that the event kernels of both processes are Markov, the two laws are probability measures, the number of live lineages of the backward process reaches at most one almost surely, the observed coalescence times are almost surely finite, and the expected number of active events, the expected total time, and the expected largest observed coalescence time are bounded by an explicit absorption budget.

recordDecisions.title: When one finite block of linked sites separates a three-sample genealogy from every panmictic history
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: This entry formalizes conditions under which a single finite block of linked sites separates a three-sample genealogy from every panmictic history. A law of the two coalescence-interval lengths and the tree shape of three sampled sequences is uniformly separated at mutation scale k > 0 when some block of L completely linked sites, observed under the equal-rates mutation model, has a law at ℓ1 distance at least a fixed ε > 0 from the block law of every panmictic history (any nonnegative, locally integrable, time-varying coalescence rate with a diverging integrated clock), at every mutation scale and for every alphabet size K ≥ 2. For laws with nonnegative interval lengths, a positive first coalescence time, and a regular first-survival profile matching the first coalescence time, uniform separation holds if and only if the law differs from the panmictic law with the profile's rate, in which the tree shape is uniform and independent of the times; a version for laws of the interval lengths alone, with a uniform independent shape, is also given. For three-sample symmetric island histories with time-varying coalescence and migration rates under the stated integrability hypotheses, uniform separation holds if and only if the history is not the one with all three lineages starting in the same island, no migration, and a diverging integrated coalescence clock. For finite-phase histories, separation is equivalent to failure of a density identity characterizing the panmictic form.
